standard.title: Local significance
standard.description: a local individual, group, place or building and the reasons for their importance, including social, cultural or spiritual significance
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y1 (AC9HS1K01-K02): Students compared family structures and daily life across generations. They understand continuity and change and comparative language.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the importance of a local individual, group, place or building, including its social, cultural or spiritual significance.

nodes.label: Types of local significance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify different types of significance (social, cultural, spiritual, historical) and give examples of each from their local area.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two types of significance and give one local example of each.
nodes.typical_width: Explore a range of local individuals, groups, places and buildings; classify each by type of significance; discuss why particular sites have heritage significance or cultural value for present generations.
wider: Identify local sites of significance to First Nations Australians (engraving sites, rock paintings, natural features) and explain their significance from a First Nations perspective
Compare why the same local site might have different significance to different community groups
nodes.hinge_reason: Without a conceptual vocabulary for types of significance, students cannot explain why a specific local place matters — the explanatory task in Node 2 requires these categories.

response_modes.reason: Social, cultural and spiritual significance are abstract at Year 2 — anchor each type to a concrete local example before asking students to classify independently.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations significance offers a qualitatively distinct type of significance (spiritual and living, not just historical) that enriches all students' understanding.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two types of significance by name
Gives at least one local example of each type

nodes.label: Investigating a local place or person
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate the history of a chosen local individual, group, place or building using provided sources and construct an account of what makes it important.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two provided sources to describe why a local place, person or building is important.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate the history of a chosen person, building, site or place using the internet, books, newspapers, community guides, photographs and audio-visual material; relate the story these sources reveal about the past; explain reasons for importance.
wider: Design a local historical tour of a building or site and develop explanatory notes for each stop
Compare two different local significant sites from different cultural groups and explain what each reveals about the community's identity

response_modes.reason: The investigation integrates source use, significance vocabulary and local knowledge into an explanatory account — it is the integration task for this standard.

success_criteria: Uses at least two sources in the investigation
Explains why the chosen place or person is important using at least one type of significance
